title: On ego
hookLine: he calls ego a deep illness with a cure inside it

lines: THE MEDICINE IS IN THERE TOO.
cards: Where would you look for the cure to an illness? The pharmacy, the doctor's, a lab somewhere. Almost never inside the illness itself.

Yesterday's salok named pride as the thing that spoils service. Today Guru Angad goes under pride to the root it grows from, what Sikhs call haumai, ego, the sense of I and mine. He gives it a hard diagnosis.
Then, in the same breath, he says something no doctor's chart would say: the medicine is in there too.

teach.b: The salok, in Asa di Var and marked Mahala two, describes ego the way you'd describe a creature's habits. This is the nature of haumai: in ego, people act. In ego they are bound, and in ego they keep coming and going.
Haumai is a long, deep illness, but its medicine is also within it. If the One shows grace, a person lives the Guru's Word. Nanak says: listen, people, this is how the troubles depart.
Three things to notice. First, he doesn't pretend ego is small. It's a long illness, deep and lasting, not a bad mood that passes by evening.
Second, he doesn't send you far away for the cure.
The medicine is within it, and readers hear that in more than one way. Some hear that the cure is inside the person who has the illness; you don't have to become someone else to heal.
Some hear that it's inside the illness itself: the same I that grabs and insists can be the I that turns and listens, its energy turned toward the Word.
Third, he names how the turning happens: grace, and then living the Guru's Word, not just knowing it, day after day. So the salok is hard and hopeful at once. Hard, because it takes ego seriously.
Hopeful, because the way out isn't somewhere you can't reach.
That's today's line: the cure inside.

how: Sikh teachers speak of haumai, ego, as a central obstacle in Gurbani, and draw on this salok from Asa di Var when they speak of its cure through the Guru's Word.

o: a healthy pride that keeps you confident and strong
haumai: a deep illness of I and mine, its cure within
a sin that only outward rituals can wash away

games.q: the salok on ego: tap the pairs.
p: ego, the sense of I and mine

s: the salok calls ego a small thing that passes quickly
it calls haumai a long, deep illness.
the salok says the medicine for ego is within it
the illness and its cure are named in the same line.
in the salok, knowing the Word is enough on its own
it speaks of grace, and of living the Guru's Word, not only knowing it.

games.q: Guru Angad has just called ego a long, deep illness. where does he say the medicine is?
o: far away, at a pilgrim site.
games.why: the medicine is within it, he says, and it works through grace and living the Guru's Word.

practice: Let the I-thoughts come up as they do, I'm right, I'm tired of this, nobody noticed what I did, I need, and instead of fighting them, label each one softly as it passes, there's the I, and let it go by.
Watch with the patience you'd give someone recovering from a long illness, and if you pray, say Waheguru on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: On ego. Guru Angad's salok: haumai is a long, deep illness, and its medicine is within it, found through grace and the Guru's Word lived out. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the cure inside. A long illness, and a medicine close at hand. Until tomorrow.
